title: openai /v1/chat.completions parity: params, roles, stop/logprobs, response formatting
author: Priya Menon
description:
Motivation: bring Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer for /v1/chat.completions to parity with expected parameters and behaviors used by downstream customers and third-party tooling. This PR standardizes parameter handling (temperature, top_p, n, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, max_tokens), clarifies role serialization (system/user/assistant), implements stop sequence semantics and logprobs passthrough, and fixes streaming response formatting so "delta" patches match OpenAI's streaming chunks.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds canonical parameter mapping and validation for chat.completions-compatible requests (preserves Redwood internal names but accepts OpenAI aliases).
- Ensures role normalization and preservation of role fields across pipelines (system -> system, user -> user, assistant -> assistant).
- Implements stop sequence behavior at both per-request and model-bridge layers and surfaces stop-based truncation metadata.
- Surfaces token-level logprobs in the compatibility response when model returns logprobs (supports top_logprobs and tokens fields).
- Reworks streaming message framing to emit OpenAI-compatible event chunks (content delta / role only when first token), including an explicit "done" / "[DONE]" terminal event.
- Adds tests covering parameter mapping, role preservation, stop sequence edge cases, and logprobs streaming.
- Updates docs and SDK shim to reflect compatibility guarantees.

Checklist:
- [x] Parameter acceptance and validation mapping (temperature, top_p, n, etc).
- [x] Role normalization and tests for mixed-role histories.
- [x] Stop sequence implementation and tests for multi-stop behavior.
- [x] Logprobs passthrough for non-streaming and streaming paths.
- [x] Streaming chunk formatting parity with OpenAI (including delta/role events).
- [x] SDK/Docs update for Python and TS shims.
- [x] CI added to catch regressions in streaming formatting.

Compatibility notes: This preserves Redwood's existing internal inference parameters but accepts OpenAI-named params in the API layer. For hosts using pinned endpoints, there is no behavioral change unless they switch to the new compatibility flag (openai_compat_version = "v1-chat-parity-2026-02"). We included a rollout plan to enable the flag by default after a one-week opt-in period to monitor error rates and client telemetry.

Testing/QA: Unit + integration tests added under tests/openai_compat/. End-to-end smoke tests run against a small dedicated canary pool; streaming formatting was validated with a local harness against a recorded OpenAI stream sample. CI initially flaked on a timing-sensitive test for streaming chunk boundaries; added a retry/time-tolerance to stabilize.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the model bridge stop/truncation logic and the streaming encoder. The streaming encoder changes are minimal but subtle: they ensure we only emit a role on the first chunk and aggregate deltas into valid JSON 'choices' objects for each SSE event. If we get sign-off we'll squash-merge and cut a short changelog entry for the API docs.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor (2026-02-16): Overall looks good. A couple of questions: 1) In chat_completions.py we accept both 'top_p' and 'topP' - prefer to canonicalize to snake_case only; 2) stop_handler currently truncates tokens at the model bridge - do we preserve full token metadata for logs?

Priya Menon (2026-02-16): Responding - we canonicalize incoming keys during API parsing and map both variants to the same internal field; added a small helper 'normalize_openai_params' to centralize this. For stop_handler we do preserve token metadata and surface a 'truncation_reason' in response metadata for audits.

Sara Huang (2026-02-17): Streaming test flaked in CI (timeout) - can we make the test tolerate small timing jitter? Also need a comment in stream_encoder about why the role is emitted only once to avoid accidental future regressions.

Priya Menon (2026-02-17): Adjusted tests to use retry-with-backoff and added detailed comment in stream_encoder. Re-ran CI and fixed an edge-case where empty assistant messages caused an extra empty chunk to be emitted.
Diego Ramirez (2026-02-18): Verified logprobs schema matches OpenAI examples for 'tokens' and 'top_logprobs'. Left one nit about formatting in docs.
Priya Menon (2026-02-19): Addressed docs nit and updated python shim with example usage. CI passing locally and on main canary; ready to merge.
release_notes: Added OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility: parameter mapping (temperature, top_p, n, penalties), role normalization, stop sequence semantics, logprobs passthrough, and streaming formatting parity. Backwards-compatible opt-in flag; default rollout planned after one-week canary.
